title: goal-lab-failure-modes-log-kenji-ito
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, private scratch for tracking the next three weeks of personal OKR experiments and the likely failure modes. Goal is to keep a very small set of measurable bets and a short failure-mode checklist so I can iterate quickly without losing context.

Context and thesis:
- Primary objective: increase reliable weekly "throughput-of-focus" (TOF) from ~8h to ~12h of uninterrupted deep work over a three-week sprint while keeping output quality steady.
- Why: I am repeatedly losing time to context switching (meetings, ad-hoc requests). If I can raise TOF by 50% while shipping same number of high-impact PRs, I expect spike in perceived velocity and fewer late surprises during rollouts.

Key success metrics (quantified, simple):
- TOF (hours/week): baseline 8, target 12. Logged daily in a simple timer.
- PR quality: % of PRs merged without rework within 48h: baseline ~60%, target >=75%.
- Interruptions: number of distinct async ask threads requiring >10m/day from me: baseline ~6/day, target <=3/day.
- Sprint output: 2x small RFCs + 1 production bugfix merged within 3 weeks.

Hypotheses (to test):
- H1: Blocking calendar mornings (9–12) will reduce context switching and increase TOF by at least 2 hours/week.
- H2: Proactively triaging a weekly "ask queue" doc on Monday will reduce ad-hoc interrupts by 30% because people have a single place to raise requests.
- H3: Pre-PR checklist (5 checklist items) will reduce rework loops for infra PRs and improve merge-without-rework rate.

Planned experiments (week-by-week):
- Week 1 (2025-02-24 to 2025-03-02): enforce no-meeting mornings Mon–Thu; start a single-line "Ask Queue" doc and ping team on Mon AM; add PR checklist to my local template. Measure TOF and interruptions.
- Week 2 (2025-03-03 to 2025-03-09): keep no-meeting mornings; schedule one 30m deep-review block Wed; iterate checklist items; log times per task.
- Week 3 (2025-03-10 to 2025-03-16): broaden experiment by inviting two teammates to adopt the Ask Queue; record effects on interrupts and PR turnaround.

Failure modes (what will make this experiment fail):
1) Social friction: team pushes back because blocking mornings creates backlog for product/CS. Mitigation: share a short note and commit to same-day email triage and 2pm office hours.
2) Over-optimization: I game TOF by doing low-value tasks in blocks. Mitigation: pair TOF with PR quality & priority points; low-value will show in PR count/impact.
3) Unplanned incidents: pager or SRE incidents will wipe out focused blocks. Mitigation: coordinate on-call handoffs, set escalation expectations, and track incident time separately.
4) Measurement noise: timers misused, TOF inflation. Mitigation: simple single-tap timer (start/stop) and end-of-day 2-line log to validate.

Quick checklist to carry forward (execute every Monday):
- [ ] Post Ask Queue link in team channel (one-line summary).
- [ ] Block calendar mornings for the week.
- [ ] Add PR checklist to any new branch.
- [ ] 15m sync with SRE if on-call that week to set escalation boundaries.

Retrospective template (end of week):
- What worked (2 bullets)
- What didn't (2 bullets)
- One small change to carry forward
- One experiment to stop

Notes from this morning (2025-02-24):
- Baseline log: TOF yesterday = 7.25h (lost 2h to last-minute design review and unplanned sync).
- Immediate tweak: set Slack status + "Do Not Disturb until 12:00" and add an auto-reply in shared Ask Queue to set expectations.

Open questions / blockers:
- Is there an existing team policy on meeting blackouts? I think Eng-Platform had a short doc but couldn't find it. (linked_artifacts includes the roadmap page; will search further.)
- Who on the team would be the best partner to pilot Ask Queue? Rina volunteered informally — ask to formalize.

Backlog ideas (potential future bets):
- Energy-weighted scheduling: track perceived energy (1–5) and schedule tasks accordingly; test if pairing high-energy slots with deep work increases TOF effectiveness.
- Micro-OKR: create a 4-line micro-OKR for infra work to experiment with smaller commitments.

Tiny admin notes for myself:
- Add PROJ-1024 to weekly review (relates to infra rollout).
- Follow up on PR #1873 feedback and update checklist accordingly.

End of note.

(Short, messy, intentionally episodic — this is a working doc, not a polished handbook.)
